exercise.name: L-Sit
steps: Grip parallel bars or press your hands into the floor beside your hips.
Push down through straight arms to lift your body.
Raise your straight legs level with your hips and hold.
exercise.one_line_summary: Hands on two parallettes beside the hips, arms straight and locked, body lifted off the floor, straight legs held level with the hips. One picture (a hold). Abs are the target; triceps press down and the thigh (rectus femoris) holds the legs up.

setup.target: Parallettes beside the hips, arms straight and vertical.
Straight, together, level with the hips.

muscles.emg: No L-sit EMG study found; nearest: V-sit ~80% MVIC RA (S3), leg raise works the abs and hip flexors (S1), hanging knee-up high RA (S2).
muscles.role: Holds the pelvis so the legs can stay up.
muscles.surface: The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, lower ribs to the pubic bone.

muscles.role: Locks the elbows and lifts the body.
muscles.surface: Back of the upper arm, shoulder to elbow.

muscles.emg: Leg raise raises hip-flexor (rectus femoris) EMG (S1).
muscles.role: Lifts and holds the straight legs; keeps the knees locked.
muscles.surface: Front of the thigh, hip to knee.

mistakes.why_it_matters: Then it is a tuck hold, not an L-sit.

sources.citation: Kim K, Lee T. 2016. Comparison of muscular activities in the abdomen and lower limbs while performing sit-up and leg-raise. J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):491-494. doi:10.1589/jpts.28.491
sources.what_it_gave: Sit-up vs leg raise (upper/lower RA, external oblique, rectus femoris, iliopsoas): the eccentric sit-up raised abdominal activity most; the leg raise and eccentric sit-up raised hip-flexor activity.

sources.citation: Escamilla RF, Babb E, DeWitt R, et al. 2006. Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. Phys Ther 86(5):656-671. doi:10.1093/ptj/86.5.656
sources.what_it_gave: Hanging knee-up with straps and the reverse crunch inclined 30 deg are among the highest for upper/lower rectus abdominis, obliques and latissimus; rectus femoris high in the inclined reverse crunch and bent-knee sit-up.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Erector spinae highest in back extensions (~63% MVIC on the floor, ~56% on a bench); V-sits ~80% MVIC rectus abdominis; adding a stability ball raises core EMG; sit-ups and curl-ups the classic core exercises.
